subject: Q4 runway rebalance: triage, commit asks & 'strafe' plan
messages:
From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
To: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>, Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwood.com>, Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.com>
Date: Thu, 21 Oct 2026 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Q4 runway rebalance: triage, commit asks & 'strafe' plan

Team —

Quick summary: finance flagged a runway tilt this morning when we reconciled bookings vs. committed run rate. We have a ~22% pipe-to-quota shortfall for Q4 at our current commit signals. Rather than broad panic, we need a focused "rebalance + strafe" play: surface small, near-term conversion opportunities, lock commit intents, and cleanse non-reps in CRM.

Attached: 2026Q4_pipeline_snapshot.xlsx (summary tab & by-owner) and run_rate_model_v3.csv. Key asks below — please do these by EOD Thursday (10/23) so we can finalize the forecast for Finance on Friday.

Action items:
- Update CRM commit status for every OPPTY with ACV >= $25k that is in Proposal/Legal/Commit stages. Mark: Commit / Commit-at-risk / No-commit. (Owner: each AE)
- For any change from Commit -> Commit-at-risk or No-commit, add a 1–2 line reason and next-step in the opportunity notes.
- Ben: prioritize outreach to the top 6 mid-market deals that can convert in 21 days (see sheet "mid-market"). Provide expected close probability and one-sentence next-step.
- Neha: re-run coverage math defending discount/credit exposure and call out any deals where Finance approval is required for concessions > 15%.
- Laura: prepare a 3-slide "rebalance playbook" summarizing who to escalate, emergency canaries, and rollback thresholds for discounts.

Important: Do not create new commit flags without a plain-English owner confirmation in the notes (email confirmations are fine). We'll use these notes as the single source for Finance verification.

If you see any legal/contract blockers, loop in Rishi. FinOps will sign off Friday morning only on a cleaned list.

Marissa
Marissa Cole
Head of GTM Ops, Redwood Inference
marissa.cole@redwood.com
+1 415-555-0123

Thanks — on it. Quick note on my slate: I pulled the "mid-market" tab and will focus on 6 deals that meet the "21-day" conversion profile. Preliminary plan:

Top 3 to push this week:
- ACME-P: $220k ARR — legal is the blocker; procurement asked for a 60-day SLA tweak. I have a call with Jamie (Acme) at 3pm PT to confirm the timeline.
- Solinux Co: $95k — internal sign-off only, expect to close with credit memo.
- BrightEdge Systems: $60k — needs final pricing approval; I think we can close with standard discount.

Requests:
- Marissa/Neha: can Finance pre-clear the ACME-P SLA tweak (small T&Cs) or do I need a formal ticket? If we need Finance approval, I need that by 2pm tomorrow to keep the Acme cadence.
- Laura: I can share a 1-pager for each of the top 3 by EOD today for the playbook slide.

On notes: I'll update CRM after the 3pm with call summary and commit intent.

Ben

Good progress — attaching a quick slide outline in the body below for the playbook. I can convert it to slides once Ben shares his 1-pagers.

Playbook outline (short):
1) Escalation matrix: who to call for legal, procurement, finance exceptions.
2) Emergency canaries: 3 deals we use to validate a rebound (ACME-P, Solinux Co, BrightEdge).
3) Discount thresholds: up to 12% AE approval; 12-20% requires FinOps; >20% escalate to CRO.
4) Rollback policy: if we exceed 18% discount exposure in aggregate, freeze new credits and run a second audit.

Next steps: I will produce a 3-slide PDF and drop in the folder by 9am PT Monday. Also — if anyone is planning a customer-facing contract change that increases T&Cs exposure, ping Legal immediately.

Laura
